name: Hardware Security
description: Skills related to the security evaluation and testing of hardware, embedded systems, and physical devices. Covers non-invasive, semi-invasive, and invasive analysis techniques. Note: no established framework (NICE/SFIA/ECSF) covers this domain. Taxonomy synthesized from CHES/COSADE academic literature, Common Criteria methodology, FIPS 140-3, and EMVCo evaluation standards.

categories.name: Embedded Systems Security
categories.description: Firmware extraction, debug interface exploitation (JTAG/SWD/UART), secure boot analysis, firmware reverse engineering, and embedded OS security.

categories.name: Side-Channel Analysis
categories.description: Power analysis (SPA/DPA/CPA), electromagnetic analysis (EMA), timing attacks, and cache-based side channels. Covers acquisition, signal processing, and statistical analysis.

categories.name: Fault Injection
categories.description: Voltage glitching, clock glitching, electromagnetic fault injection (EMFI), and laser fault injection. Covers glitch parameter optimization, fault models, and combined attacks.

categories.name: Invasive Analysis
categories.description: Chip decapsulation, delayering, microprobing, FIB (focused ion beam) circuit editing, and optical/electron microscopy analysis.

categories.name: PCB Reverse Engineering
categories.description: Component identification, schematic reconstruction, bus analysis and sniffing, test point identification, and PCB-level modification.

categories.name: RF & Wireless (On-Device)
categories.description: On-device RF analysis: RFID/NFC chip security, hardware radio transceiver evaluation, antenna analysis, and RF emission characterization at the hardware level.

categories.name: Cryptographic Implementation Assessment
categories.description: Review of cryptographic algorithm implementations in hardware. Covers RNG evaluation, key management in hardware, HSM assessment, and crypto accelerator analysis.

categories.name: Sample Preparation
categories.description: Physical and chemical preparation of IC and hardware samples for analysis. Covers mechanical preparation (mounting, cross-sectioning, polishing), chemical handling and safety, and goal-specific preparation for optical imaging, SEM/FIB imaging, and active analysis (fault injection, probing, FIB editing) where device functionality must be preserved.
